title: Flow Designer Transaction Boundaries: What Every ServiceNow Developer Must Know
excerpt: Flow Designer executes asynchronously with no native rollback. Learn how transactions commit, when to use business rules instead, and proven compensating transaction patterns for production workflows.
content:
Understanding Flow Designer's Execution Model

Flow Designer runs in the background with always a delay between trigger and execution start. Each database operation commits separately—there is no built-in transaction rollback across multiple actions, unlike legacy Workflow Editor.

Critical Design Decision

Use business rules when you need "ON BEFORE" execution or must run in the same thread as database operations. Flow Designer cannot execute before database writes.

Transaction Commit Timing

Each Flow Designer action that writes to the database commits independently. This means if Action 3 fails after Actions 1 and 2 succeed, those earlier writes persist.

// Flow execution timeline:
// Trigger: Incident created (committed)
// Action 1: Update CI (commits immediately)
// Action 2: Create Task (commits immediately)
// Action 3: REST call fails → Actions 1 & 2 already committed

Error Handler Propagation Rules

Error handlers can be configured at flow and subflow levels:

  • If a subflow has an error handler, it handles the error locally
  • Otherwise, the error propagates to the main flow's handler
  • Unhandled errors terminate the flow but don't rollback prior commits

Compensating Transaction Patterns

Since native rollback doesn't exist, implement compensating transactions:

// Pattern: Track changes for potential rollback
var CompensatingTxn = Class.create();
CompensatingTxn.prototype = {
  initialize: function(flowExecutionId) {
    this.changes = [];
    this.flowId = flowExecutionId;
  },
  
  recordChange: function(table, sysId, field, oldValue) {
    this.changes.push({
      table: table,
      sys_id: sysId,
      field: field,
      original: oldValue,
      timestamp: new GlideDateTime()
    });
  },
  
  rollback: function() {
    for (var i = this.changes.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
      var change = this.changes[i];
      var gr = new GlideRecord(change.table);
      if (gr.get(change.sys_id)) {
        gr.setValue(change.field, change.original);
        gr.setWorkflow(false);
        gr.update();
      }
    }
  },
  type: 'CompensatingTxn'
};

When to Use Business Rules Instead

ScenarioUse Business RuleUse Flow Designer
Must run before DB write✓ Before BR✗
Same transaction required✓✗
Long-running process✗✓ Async
Multi-step orchestration✗✓
High-volume triggers✓ Less overheadConsider carefully

Best Practices

  • Design flows to be idempotent—safe to retry
  • Log state transitions for audit and debugging
  • Use subflows with local error handlers for isolation
  • Consider saga pattern for complex multi-system workflows
  • Test failure scenarios explicitly in ATF

title: Scoped Application Security Patterns: Cross-Scope Access Done Right
excerpt: Navigate ServiceNow's scoped application security model with confidence. Learn cross-scope access patterns, ACL evaluation order, and security best practices for enterprise applications.
content:
ACL Evaluation Order

ACLs evaluate from most specific to least specific:

  1. Field-level on specific table
  2. Table-level on specific table
  3. Field-level wildcard
  4. Table-level wildcard

Critical: All applicable ACLs must pass for access to be granted. Each ACL rule can contain Required Roles, Condition filters, and Scripts—all three must evaluate to true.

GlideRecordSecure vs GlideRecord

// GlideRecordSecure automatically enforces ACLs
var grs = new GlideRecordSecure('incident');
grs.query();
while (grs.next()) {
  // Only returns records user can read
}

// GlideRecord requires manual checks
var gr = new GlideRecord('incident');
gr.query();
while (gr.next()) {
  if (gr.canRead()) {
    // Safe to display
  }
}

Default to GlideRecordSecure unless explicitly bypassing ACLs is required.

Cross-Scope Access Patterns

Scoped applications isolate custom tables, scripts, and configurations from global scope. Cross-scope access requires explicit grants.

// In your scoped Script Include, check caller's scope
var CallerValidator = Class.create();
CallerValidator.prototype = {
  initialize: function() {},
  
  validateCrossScope: function(allowedScopes) {
    var callerScope = gs.getCurrentScopeName();
    if (allowedScopes.indexOf(callerScope) === -1) {
      gs.warn('Unauthorized cross-scope access from: ' + callerScope);
      return false;
    }
    return true;
  },
  
  type: 'CallerValidator'
};

Script Include Access Control

  • Mark Script Includes as Client Callable only when necessary
  • Prefer server-side calls over client-callable endpoints
  • Validate inputs in all client-callable methods
// Secure client-callable Script Include pattern
var SecureAPI = Class.create();
SecureAPI.prototype = Object.extendsObject(AbstractAjaxProcessor, {
  
  getData: function() {
    // Always validate role
    if (!gs.hasRole('x_app_scope.user')) {
      return JSON.stringify({error: 'Access denied'});
    }
    
    // Validate and sanitize input
    var inputId = this.getParameter('sysparm_id');
    if (!this._isValidSysId(inputId)) {
      return JSON.stringify({error: 'Invalid input'});
    }
    
    // Use GlideRecordSecure
    var grs = new GlideRecordSecure('x_app_scope_table');
    if (grs.get(inputId)) {
      return JSON.stringify({
        name: grs.getValue('name'),
        status: grs.getValue('status')
      });
    }
    return JSON.stringify({error: 'Not found'});
  },
  
  _isValidSysId: function(id) {
    return id && /^[a-f0-9]{32}$/.test(id);
  },
  
  type: 'SecureAPI'
});

Application Cross-Scope Access Records

Configure in System Applications > Cross-Scope Access:

  • Define which external scopes can access your tables
  • Specify allowed operations (read, write, create, delete)
  • Grant Script Include access to specific scopes

Security Anti-Patterns to Avoid

  • Using gs.setSession() to bypass ACLs
  • Hardcoding admin credentials in integrations
  • Making all Script Includes client-callable
  • Storing sensitive data in client-accessible fields
  • Using eval() or dynamic script execution

title: Predictive Intelligence Deep Dive: Requirements, Limitations, and Production Patterns
excerpt: Predictive Intelligence requires minimum 10,000 records for classification training. Learn the real requirements, common misconceptions, and patterns for production ML implementations.
content:
Predictive Intelligence Components

The framework includes four components:

  • Classification: Auto-categorization of records
  • Similarity: Finding related records
  • Clustering: Pattern identification
  • Regression: Numerical prediction

Critical Training Requirements

Classification requires minimum 10,000 records for training. This is non-negotiable for production-quality models.

Model TypeMinimum RecordsRecommended
Classification10,00050,000+
Similarity1,00010,000+
Clustering5,00025,000+

Common Misconception: Major Incident Prediction

Major incident detection uses similarity models to find tickets similar to existing major incidents—it does NOT predict new major incidents. This is a frequent misunderstanding.

// What it actually does:
// 1. New incident created
// 2. Similarity model compares to past major incidents
// 3. If similar, flags for review
// 4. Human confirms or rejects

// What it does NOT do:
// Predict that a new, unique issue will become a major incident

Training Data Quality

Model accuracy depends heavily on data quality:

  • Clean, consistent categorization in historical data
  • Remove spam, test, and duplicate records before training
  • Ensure balanced class distribution
  • Regular retraining as data patterns evolve
// Pre-training data cleanup script
var cleanup = new GlideRecord('incident');
cleanup.addQuery('short_description', 'CONTAINS', 'test');
cleanup.addQuery('sys_created_by', 'admin');
cleanup.query();

while (cleanup.next()) {
  cleanup.u_exclude_from_training = true;
  cleanup.update();
}

// Verify class distribution
var ga = new GlideAggregate('incident');
ga.addQuery('u_exclude_from_training', false);
ga.addAggregate('COUNT');
ga.groupBy('category');
ga.query();

while (ga.next()) {
  gs.info(ga.category + ': ' + ga.getAggregate('COUNT'));
}

Production Deployment Pattern

  1. Shadow mode first: Run predictions without auto-applying
  2. Measure accuracy: Compare predictions to actual assignments
  3. Set confidence threshold: Only auto-apply above 85%+ confidence
  4. Human review queue: Route low-confidence predictions for manual review
  5. Feedback loop: Use corrections to improve the model
// Flow Designer pattern for confidence-based routing
// In a Script step:
var confidence = parseFloat(inputs.pi_confidence) || 0;

if (confidence >= 0.85) {
  outputs.auto_apply = true;
  outputs.route_to = 'auto_assignment';
} else if (confidence >= 0.6) {
  outputs.auto_apply = false;
  outputs.route_to = 'human_review_queue';
} else {
  outputs.auto_apply = false;
  outputs.route_to = 'manual_triage';
}

Model Retraining Schedule

  • Monthly retraining for active models
  • Immediate retraining after major process changes
  • Monitor accuracy metrics weekly
  • Archive old model versions for comparison

title: Yokohama MFA Enforcement: What You Need to Know Before Upgrading
excerpt: Multi-factor authentication is mandatory in Yokohama with a 90-day grace period. Here's everything you need to configure before upgrading to avoid authentication lockouts.
content:
Critical Breaking Change

Multi-factor authentication is enabled and required by default for all local login users starting with Yokohama. This is not optional.

90-Day Grace Period

For the first 90 days after upgrade, all internal users (without snc_external role) must use MFA. Plan your rollout accordingly.

Pre-Upgrade Checklist

  1. Audit current authentication: Identify all local login users
  2. Configure MFA policies: Set up before upgrade, not after
  3. Test in non-prod: Clone production and test MFA flows
  4. Communicate to users: Announce MFA requirement 2-4 weeks before upgrade
  5. Prepare support: Expect increased help desk volume
// Audit script: Find users who will need MFA
var users = new GlideRecord('sys_user');
users.addActiveQuery();
users.addQuery('source', 'NULL').addOrCondition('source', '');
users.addQuery('roles', 'NOT LIKE', 'snc_external');
users.query();

var count = 0;
while (users.next()) {
  gs.info('Local user requiring MFA: ' + users.user_name);
  count++;
}
gs.info('Total users requiring MFA: ' + count);

Workaround for Security Pop-up

To dismiss the security enforcement pop-up after acknowledging the requirement:

// Set this property to true
gs.setProperty('glide.authenticate.multifactor.enforcement.acknowledged', 'true');

MFA Configuration Best Practices

  • Support multiple MFA methods (authenticator app, SMS, email)
  • Configure backup codes for account recovery
  • Set up MFA exemptions for service accounts (with compensating controls)
  • Document MFA enrollment process for users

Service Account Considerations

Integration and service accounts present unique challenges:

  • Use OAuth 2.0 instead of basic auth where possible
  • For basic auth integrations, use dedicated service accounts with IP restrictions
  • Document all service accounts and their authentication methods
  • Review integration credentials quarterly
// Identify service accounts for MFA planning
var svcAccounts = new GlideRecord('sys_user');
svcAccounts.addActiveQuery();
svcAccounts.addQuery('user_name', 'STARTSWITH', 'svc_')
  .addOrCondition('user_name', 'STARTSWITH', 'api_')
  .addOrCondition('user_name', 'STARTSWITH', 'integration_');
svcAccounts.query();

while (svcAccounts.next()) {
  gs.info('Service account: ' + svcAccounts.user_name + 
    ' | Last login: ' + svcAccounts.last_login_time);
}

Post-Upgrade Validation

  • Test login flows for all user types
  • Verify integrations still authenticate
  • Monitor authentication failures in logs
  • Have rollback plan ready for first 48 hours

title: Upgrade Regression Testing Framework: ATF Patterns for ServiceNow Customizations
excerpt: Build a comprehensive automated testing framework for ServiceNow upgrades. Learn ATF patterns, test suite organization, and CI/CD integration for confident upgrades.
content:
Why Upgrade Testing Fails

Most upgrade issues stem from untested customizations. ServiceNow's Automated Test Framework (ATF) provides the foundation, but requires deliberate test design.

Test Suite Organization

Structure tests by risk and function:

  • Smoke Suite: Core functionality (5-10 min)
  • Regression Suite: All customizations (30-60 min)
  • Integration Suite: External system connections (15-30 min)
  • Performance Suite: Load and response times (variable)
// Create test suite programmatically
var suite = new GlideRecord('sys_atf_test_suite');
suite.initialize();
suite.name = 'Post-Upgrade Smoke Suite';
suite.description = 'Critical path tests for upgrade validation';
suite.active = true;
var suiteSysId = suite.insert();

// Add tests to suite
var testIds = ['test1_sys_id', 'test2_sys_id', 'test3_sys_id'];
testIds.forEach(function(testId, index) {
  var member = new GlideRecord('sys_atf_test_suite_test');
  member.initialize();
  member.test_suite = suiteSysId;
  member.test = testId;
  member.order = (index + 1) * 100;
  member.insert();
});

Critical Test Patterns

1. Business Rule Validation

// Test: Business rule fires and updates correctly
// Step 1: Create test record
// Step 2: Assert field values
// Step 3: Update trigger field
// Step 4: Assert business rule result

2. ACL Verification

// Test: User with role X can access record
// Step 1: Impersonate user with specific role
// Step 2: Query target table
// Step 3: Assert record is accessible
// Step 4: Assert restricted fields are hidden

3. Integration Endpoint Testing

// Test: REST API returns expected response
// Step 1: Call Scripted REST API
// Step 2: Assert HTTP 200 status
// Step 3: Validate response schema
// Step 4: Verify data accuracy

Pre-Upgrade Test Run

  1. Run full regression suite on production clone
  2. Document all failures with screenshots
  3. Fix critical failures before upgrade
  4. Accept or defer non-critical issues

Post-Upgrade Validation Script

// Trigger ATF suite and monitor results
var runner = new sn_atf.AutomatedTestingAPI();
var suiteId = 'your_suite_sys_id';

// Start suite execution
var executionId = runner.startSuite(suiteId);
gs.info('ATF execution started: ' + executionId);

// Poll for completion (in scheduled job)
function checkResults(executionId) {
  var exec = new GlideRecord('sys_atf_test_suite_result');
  if (exec.get(executionId)) {
    if (exec.status == 'complete') {
      var passed = exec.tests_passed;
      var failed = exec.tests_failed;
      gs.info('Suite complete: ' + passed + ' passed, ' + failed + ' failed');
      
      if (failed > 0) {
        // Trigger alert
        gs.eventQueue('upgrade.test.failures', exec, failed, '');
      }
    }
  }
}

CI/CD Integration

  • Trigger ATF suites from deployment pipelines
  • Gate promotions on test passage
  • Archive results for audit trail
  • Send notifications on failures

Maintenance Best Practices

  • Review and update tests quarterly
  • Remove tests for deprecated functionality
  • Add tests for new customizations immediately
  • Track test coverage metrics

title: Now Assist Consumption Optimization: Managing Your 'Assists' Budget
excerpt: Now Assist uses a consumption-based 'assists' model with Pro Plus licensing. Learn strategies to optimize usage, monitor consumption, and maximize ROI from your AI investment.
content:
Understanding Now Assist Licensing

Now Assist requires Pro Plus or Enterprise Plus licenses across ITSM, CSM, and HRSD—approximately a 60% premium over standard Professional licenses.

The consumption model charges per "assist"—each AI-generated summary, suggestion, or action counts against your allocation.

What Counts as an Assist?

  • Incident/case summarization
  • Knowledge article suggestions
  • Resolution recommendations
  • Email draft generation
  • Code suggestions in Studio
  • Virtual Agent AI responses

Consumption Monitoring

// Query assist usage (example table structure)
var usage = new GlideAggregate('now_assist_usage');
usage.addAggregate('COUNT');
usage.addQuery('sys_created_on', '>=', gs.monthsAgo(1));
usage.groupBy('assist_type');
usage.groupBy('user');
usage.query();

while (usage.next()) {
  gs.info(usage.assist_type + ' by ' + usage.user + 
    ': ' + usage.getAggregate('COUNT'));
}

Optimization Strategies

1. Target High-Value Use Cases

Focus assists on scenarios with measurable ROI:

  • Complex incidents with long resolution times
  • Customer-facing communications
  • Knowledge creation from resolved tickets
  • Code reviews in development

2. Implement Usage Guardrails

// Business rule to limit assists per user per day
var UserAssistLimit = Class.create();
UserAssistLimit.prototype = {
  initialize: function(userId) {
    this.userId = userId;
    this.dailyLimit = parseInt(gs.getProperty('now_assist.daily_limit', '50'));
  },
  
  canUseAssist: function() {
    var today = new GlideDateTime();
    today.setDisplayValue(today.getDate().toString());
    
    var ga = new GlideAggregate('now_assist_usage');
    ga.addQuery('user', this.userId);
    ga.addQuery('sys_created_on', '>=', today);
    ga.addAggregate('COUNT');
    ga.query();
    
    if (ga.next()) {
      return parseInt(ga.getAggregate('COUNT')) < this.dailyLimit;
    }
    return true;
  },
  
  type: 'UserAssistLimit'
};

3. Cache Common Responses

For frequently asked questions, cache AI responses rather than regenerating:

  • Knowledge article suggestions for common issues
  • Standard response templates
  • Categorization for known patterns

4. Role-Based Access

Limit Now Assist features by role:

  • Full access for senior agents handling complex issues
  • Limited access for L1 support
  • Read-only for training purposes

ROI Tracking

Measure the value of your assist consumption:

  • Time saved: Compare resolution times with/without AI
  • Quality improvement: Customer satisfaction scores
  • Deflection rate: Self-service success with AI search
  • Agent productivity: Tickets handled per agent
// Calculate ROI metrics
var metrics = {
  avgResolutionWithAI: 0,
  avgResolutionWithoutAI: 0,
  assistsUsed: 0,
  costPerAssist: 0.50 // Example cost
};

// Time saved = (avgWithoutAI - avgWithAI) * ticketsProcessed
// Value = timeSaved * avgAgentHourlyRate
// ROI = (Value - (assistsUsed * costPerAssist)) / (assistsUsed * costPerAssist)

Quarterly Review Process

  1. Export usage by feature and user
  2. Identify low-value high-consumption patterns
  3. Adjust access and limits
  4. Retrain users on optimal usage
  5. Update ROI projections

title: ServiceNow for Financial Services: SOX, PCI-DSS, and Basel III Implementation Guide
excerpt: Implement ServiceNow in regulated financial environments with proven patterns for SOX compliance, PCI-DSS controls, and Basel III operational risk management.
content:
Financial Services Operations (FSO) Overview

ServiceNow FSO provides purpose-built solutions:

  • Banking: Loan origination, dispute resolution (Visa integration), payment operations
  • Insurance: Claims processing, ACORD-compliant data model
  • Investment: Trade operations workflows

SOX Compliance Implementation

ServiceNow's GRC module delivers proven SOX results:

  • 66% reduction in quarterly control certification time
  • 90% reduction in external auditor coordination
  • $500,000 annual savings (ServiceNow internal data)

Control Testing Automation

// Automated Control Testing (ACT) pattern
var ControlTest = Class.create();
ControlTest.prototype = {
  initialize: function(controlId) {
    this.control = new GlideRecord('sn_grc_control');
    this.control.get(controlId);
  },
  
  executeTest: function() {
    var testResult = {
      control_id: this.control.getUniqueValue(),
      test_date: new GlideDateTime(),
      status: 'pass',
      evidence: []
    };
    
    // Example: Test segregation of duties
    if (this.control.getValue('control_type') == 'sod') {
      testResult = this._testSegregationOfDuties(testResult);
    }
    
    this._recordResult(testResult);
    return testResult;
  },
  
  _testSegregationOfDuties: function(result) {
    // Query for users with conflicting roles
    var users = new GlideRecord('sys_user_has_role');
    users.addQuery('role.name', 'IN', 'approver,requestor');
    users.query();
    
    var conflicts = {};
    while (users.next()) {
      var userId = users.getValue('user');
      if (!conflicts[userId]) conflicts[userId] = [];
      conflicts[userId].push(users.role.name.toString());
    }
    
    for (var id in conflicts) {
      if (conflicts[id].length > 1) {
        result.status = 'fail';
        result.evidence.push('User ' + id + ' has conflicting roles');
      }
    }
    return result;
  },
  
  type: 'ControlTest'
};

PCI-DSS Controls

ServiceNow platform is PCI DSS compliant since 2023. Key implementation patterns:

  • Requirement 7: Restrict access using ACLs and roles
  • Requirement 8: MFA enforcement (mandatory in Yokohama)
  • Requirement 10: Audit logging via sys_audit
  • Requirement 12: Policy management in GRC
// PCI audit trail verification
var audit = new GlideRecord('sys_audit');
audit.addQuery('tablename', 'IN', 'cmdb_ci_server,sys_user,change_request');
audit.addQuery('sys_created_on', '>=', gs.daysAgo(90));
audit.addQuery('fieldname', 'IN', 'password,credentials,api_key');
audit.query();

gs.info('Sensitive field changes in last 90 days: ' + audit.getRowCount());

Basel III Operational Risk

Implement Operational Risk Management for:

  • Capital adequacy monitoring
  • Liquidity risk management
  • Regulatory reporting automation

Risk Event Capture

// Operational risk event from incident
function createRiskEvent(incident) {
  var risk = new GlideRecord('sn_grc_risk_event');
  risk.initialize();
  risk.short_description = 'Operational loss: ' + incident.short_description;
  risk.risk_category = mapToBaselCategory(incident.category);
  risk.financial_impact = calculateImpact(incident);
  risk.source_record = incident.getUniqueValue();
  risk.insert();
}

function mapToBaselCategory(incidentCategory) {
  var mapping = {
    'hardware': 'business_disruption',
    'software': 'execution_delivery',
    'security': 'external_fraud'
  };
  return mapping[incidentCategory] || 'other';
}

Regulatory Reporting Dashboard

Build executive dashboards showing:

  • Control effectiveness trends
  • Open findings by severity
  • Audit timeline and status
  • Risk heat maps by business unit

title: ServiceNow Healthcare Implementation: HIPAA, EMR Integration, and Clinical Workflows
excerpt: Build HIPAA-compliant ServiceNow implementations with EMR integration patterns, clinical device management, and healthcare-specific workflow automation.
content:
HIPAA Compliance Foundation

ServiceNow maintains HITRUST CSF certification and enters Business Associate Agreements (BAAs) with covered entities.

Security Controls Required

  • Encryption: At-rest (AES-256) and in-transit (TLS 1.2+)
  • Access Control: Role-based with MFA (mandatory in Yokohama)
  • Audit Trails: All PHI access logged in sys_audit
  • Data Minimization: Collect only necessary PHI

EMR Integration Patterns

Epic and Cerner integrations enable single-click issue reporting from clinical workflows, saving 7 minutes average per incident report.

// EMR Help integration pattern
var EMRIntegration = Class.create();
EMRIntegration.prototype = {
  initialize: function(emrType) {
    this.emrType = emrType; // 'epic' or 'cerner'
    this.endpoint = gs.getProperty('emr.' + emrType + '.endpoint');
  },
  
  createIncidentFromEMR: function(emrContext) {
    var inc = new GlideRecord('incident');
    inc.initialize();
    inc.short_description = 'EMR Issue: ' + emrContext.error_code;
    inc.description = this._buildDescription(emrContext);
    inc.caller_id = this._lookupUser(emrContext.user_id);
    inc.u_emr_context = JSON.stringify(emrContext);
    inc.category = 'clinical_systems';
    inc.subcategory = this.emrType;
    
    // Auto-assignment based on EMR module
    inc.assignment_group = this._getAssignmentGroup(emrContext.module);
    
    return inc.insert();
  },
  
  _buildDescription: function(ctx) {
    // Sanitize PHI from error context
    var sanitized = this._removePHI(ctx);
    return 'Module: ' + ctx.module + '\n' +
           'Error: ' + ctx.error_code + '\n' +
           'Timestamp: ' + ctx.timestamp;
  },
  
  _removePHI: function(ctx) {
    // Remove patient identifiers
    delete ctx.patient_mrn;
    delete ctx.patient_name;
    delete ctx.dob;
    return ctx;
  },
  
  type: 'EMRIntegration'
};

Clinical Device Management (CDM)

Track medical device lifecycle with compliance dashboards for JCAHO, CMS, and FDA requirements.

// Medical device compliance check
var deviceCompliance = new GlideRecord('cmdb_ci_medical_device');
deviceCompliance.addQuery('next_maintenance', '<', gs.daysAgo(-30));
deviceCompliance.addQuery('fda_class', 'IN', 'II,III');
deviceCompliance.query();

while (deviceCompliance.next()) {
  // Create compliance task
  var task = new GlideRecord('task');
  task.initialize();
  task.short_description = 'Overdue maintenance: ' + deviceCompliance.name;
  task.cmdb_ci = deviceCompliance.getUniqueValue();
  task.priority = deviceCompliance.fda_class == 'III' ? 1 : 2;
  task.assignment_group = deviceCompliance.support_group;
  task.insert();
}

Healthcare Workflow Patterns

Patient Experience Requests

  • Room temperature/lighting adjustments
  • Dietary requests
  • Family communication needs
  • Equipment requests

Clinical Support Requests

  • Lab result inquiries
  • Pharmacy consultations
  • Care coordination
  • Discharge planning

Success Metrics

Healthcare implementations report:

  • Omnicare: 90% first-contact resolution
  • Orbita: 70% reduction in nurse response times
  • Average: 7 minutes saved per incident report with EMR integration

title: ServiceNow Manufacturing: OT/IT Convergence and Connected Operations
excerpt: Implement ServiceNow for manufacturing with OT/IT convergence patterns, IoT integration, and field service optimization for Industry 4.0 environments.
content:
Operational Technology Management

Launched at Knowledge 2021, OT Management centralizes IT and OT assets in a single CMDB using ISA-95 equipment model standards.

OT Asset Discovery

Service Graph Connectors integrate with:

  • Claroty (OT security)
  • Nozomi Networks (OT visibility)
  • Forescout (device visibility)
// OT asset normalization pattern
var OTAssetSync = Class.create();
OTAssetSync.prototype = {
  initialize: function(source) {
    this.source = source;
    this.mapping = this._loadMapping();
  },
  
  syncAsset: function(otData) {
    var ci = new GlideRecord('cmdb_ci_ot_device');
    
    // Check for existing CI
    ci.addQuery('u_ot_device_id', otData.device_id);
    ci.query();
    
    if (!ci.next()) {
      ci.initialize();
    }
    
    // Map OT data to CMDB fields
    ci.name = otData.device_name;
    ci.u_ot_device_id = otData.device_id;
    ci.u_isa95_level = this._mapISA95Level(otData.level);
    ci.u_protocol = otData.protocol; // Modbus, OPC-UA, etc.
    ci.location = this._resolveLocation(otData.zone);
    ci.u_criticality = this._assessCriticality(otData);
    
    if (ci.isNewRecord()) {
      return ci.insert();
    } else {
      return ci.update();
    }
  },
  
  _mapISA95Level: function(level) {
    // ISA-95 levels: 0-4
    // 0: Physical process
    // 1: Sensing/manipulating
    // 2: Monitoring/supervisory

Standard Relationship Types

Parent RelationshipChild RelationshipUse Case

REST API Relationship Creation

  "attributes": {
    "name": "ORCL01",
    "version": "19c",
    "install_status": "1"
  },
  "outbound_relations": [{
    "type": "5f985e0ec0a8010e00a9714f2a172815", // Runs on::Runs sys_id
    "target": "a1b2c3d4e5f6789012345678abcdef01"  // Windows server sys_id
  }]
}

GlideRecord Relationship Creation

// Create CI with relationship using GlideRecord
function createCIWithRelationship(ciData, relationshipData) {
  // 1. Create the CI
  var ci = new GlideRecord(ciData.table);
  ci.initialize();
  ci.name = ciData.name;
  ci.install_status = ciData.status || 1;
  var ciSysId = ci.insert();
  
  // 2. Create the relationship
  var rel = new GlideRecord('cmdb_rel_ci');
  rel.initialize();
  rel.type = relationshipData.type_sys_id;
  
  if (relationshipData.direction == 'outbound') {
    rel.parent = ciSysId;
    rel.child = relationshipData.target_sys_id;
  } else {
    rel.parent = relationshipData.target_sys_id;
    rel.child = ciSysId;
  }
  
  rel.insert();
  return ciSysId;
}

// Usage example
var newCI = createCIWithRelationship(
  { table: 'cmdb_ci_appl', name: 'MyApp', status: 1 },
  { type_sys_id: 'runs_on_sys_id', direction: 'outbound', target_sys_id: 'server_sys_id' }
);

Querying Relationships

// Find all CIs that a service depends on
function getServiceDependencies(serviceSysId) {
  var deps = [];
  var rel = new GlideRecord('cmdb_rel_ci');
  rel.addQuery('parent', serviceSysId);
  rel.addQuery('type.name', 'Depends on::Used by');
  rel.query();
  
  while (rel.next()) {
    var childCI = rel.child.getRefRecord();
    deps.push({
      sys_id: childCI.getUniqueValue(),
      name: childCI.getValue('name'),
      class: childCI.getValue('sys_class_name')
    });
  }
  return deps;
}

// Find impact path (what depends on this CI)
function getImpactedServices(ciSysId, depth) {
  depth = depth || 3;
  var impacted = [];
  
  function traverse(currentId, currentDepth) {
    if (currentDepth > depth) return;
    
    var rel = new GlideRecord('cmdb_rel_ci');
    rel.addQuery('child', currentId);
    rel.addQuery('type.name', 'Depends on::Used by');
    rel.query();
    
    while (rel.next()) {
      var parentCI = rel.parent.getRefRecord();
      impacted.push({
        sys_id: parentCI.getUniqueValue(),
        name: parentCI.getValue('name'),
        depth: currentDepth
      });
      traverse(parentCI.getUniqueValue(), currentDepth + 1);
    }
  }
  
  traverse(ciSysId, 1);
  return impacted;
}

title: Integration Retry Patterns: Exponential Backoff and Error Handling
excerpt: Build resilient ServiceNow integrations with proper retry patterns, exponential backoff, and intelligent error handling for common HTTP failures.
content:
Common HTTP Errors and Solutions

CodeErrorAction
408/504TimeoutRetry with exponential backoff
401UnauthorizedRefresh OAuth tokens, verify credentials
429Rate LimitedBackoff, check rate limits
500-503Server ErrorRetry with backoff, check server logs
400Bad RequestDon't retry - fix request
404Not FoundDon't retry - verify endpoint

Exponential Backoff Implementation

var RetryHandler = Class.create();
RetryHandler.prototype = {
  initialize: function(config) {
    this.maxRetries = config.maxRetries || 3;
    this.baseDelay = config.baseDelay || 1000; // 1 second
    this.maxDelay = config.maxDelay || 30000;  // 30 seconds
  },
  
  executeWithRetry: function(restMessage) {
    var attempts = 0;
    var lastError = null;
    
    while (attempts < this.maxRetries) {
      try {
        var response = restMessage.execute();
        var status = response.getStatusCode();
        
        // Success
        if (status >= 200 && status < 300) {
          return { success: true, response: response };
        }
        
        // Don't retry client errors (except 429)
        if (status >= 400 && status < 500 && status != 429) {
          return { 
            success: false, 
            error: 'Client error: ' + status,
            response: response
          };
        }
        
        // Retry server errors and rate limits
        lastError = 'HTTP ' + status;
        attempts++;
        
        if (attempts < this.maxRetries) {
          var delay = this._calculateDelay(attempts, status, response);
          this._wait(delay);
        }
        
      } catch (e) {
        lastError = e.message;
        attempts++;
        
        if (attempts < this.maxRetries) {
          var delay = this._calculateDelay(attempts);
          this._wait(delay);
        }
      }
    }
    
    return { success: false, error: 'Max retries exceeded: ' + lastError };
  },
  
  _calculateDelay: function(attempt, status, response) {
    // Check for Retry-After header
    if (response && status == 429) {
      var retryAfter = response.getHeader('Retry-After');
      if (retryAfter) {
        return parseInt(retryAfter) * 1000;
      }
    }
    
    // Exponential backoff with jitter
    var exponentialDelay = this.baseDelay * Math.pow(2, attempt - 1);
    var jitter = Math.random() * 1000;
    return Math.min(exponentialDelay + jitter, this.maxDelay);
  },
  
  _wait: function(ms) {
    // Note: gs.sleep() should only be used in async contexts
    gs.sleep(ms);
  },
  
  type: 'RetryHandler'
};

// Usage
var retry = new RetryHandler({ maxRetries: 3, baseDelay: 2000 });
var rm = new sn_ws.RESTMessageV2('My_API', 'POST');
rm.setRequestBody(JSON.stringify(data));

var result = retry.executeWithRetry(rm);
if (result.success) {
  gs.info('Success: ' + result.response.getBody());
} else {
  gs.error('Failed: ' + result.error);
}

Flow Designer Retry Policies

Flow Designer supports retry policies for JDBC, REST, and SOAP steps:

  • Configure max attempts
  • Set delay between retries
  • Define retry conditions

Circuit Breaker Pattern

var CircuitBreaker = Class.create();
CircuitBreaker.prototype = {
  initialize: function(serviceName) {
    this.serviceName = serviceName;
    this.failureThreshold = 5;
    this.resetTimeout = 60000; // 1 minute
  },
  
  canExecute: function() {
    var state = this._getState();
    
    if (state.status == 'open') {
      // Check if reset timeout has passed
      var now = new GlideDateTime().getNumericValue();
      if (now - state.lastFailure > this.resetTimeout) {
        this._setState('half-open');
        return true;
      }
      return false;
    }
    return true;
  },
  
  recordSuccess: function() {
    this._setState('closed');
    this._resetFailures();
  },
  
  recordFailure: function() {
    var failures = this._incrementFailures();
    if (failures >= this.failureThreshold) {
      this._setState('open');
    }
  },
  
  type: 'CircuitBreaker'
};

title: Scripting Decision Framework: When to Use Business Rules vs Flow Designer
excerpt: Make the right choice between Business Rules, Flow Designer, UI Policies, and other scripting options. Includes a decision matrix and performance considerations.
content:
Decision Matrix

NeedSolutionWhy
Modify record before saveBefore Business RuleSame transaction, can abort
Update related records immediatelyAfter Business RuleSynchronous, same user session
Long-running task after saveAsync Business RuleNon-blocking, separate transaction
Show/hide fields dynamicallyUI PolicyDeclarative, no code needed
Complex client calculationsClient ScriptBrowser-side logic
Reusable server-side codeScript IncludeEncapsulation, testability
Multi-step workflow automationFlow DesignerVisual, maintainable
Recurring background tasksScheduled JobTime-based execution

Performance Considerations

Key insight: Flow Designer has more overhead than business rules. For high-volume scenarios (thousands of triggers daily), business rules perform better.

When to Avoid Flow Designer

  • Simple field updates on every insert/update
  • High-volume tables (>10,000 records/day)
  • When millisecond response time matters
  • Simple synchronous operations

When Flow Designer Excels

  • Complex multi-step processes
  • Approval workflows
  • External system orchestration
  • Non-technical maintainability required
  • Visual documentation needed

Business Rule Best Practices

// Always enclose script in functions - prevents variable leakage
(function executeRule(current, previous) {
  
  // Check conditions first (fail fast)
  if (!current.assignment_group.nil()) {
    return;
  }
  
  // Avoid current.update() in After rules - causes recursion
  // If you must update, use setWorkflow(false)
  
  // Use Script Include for complex logic
  var router = new IncidentRouter();
  var group = router.determineGroup(current);
  
  if (group) {
    current.assignment_group = group;
  }
  
})(current, previous);

UI Policy vs Client Script

// Prefer UI Policy for:
// - Show/hide fields
// - Make fields mandatory/read-only
// - Simple field clearing

// Use Client Script for:
// - Complex calculations
// - AJAX calls to server
// - Multi-field dependencies
// - Custom validation messages

// Client Script example - complex validation
function onChange(control, oldValue, newValue, isLoading) {
  if (isLoading) return;
  
  // Complex date validation
  var startDate = g_form.getValue('start_date');
  var endDate = g_form.getValue('end_date');
  
  if (startDate && endDate) {
    var start = new Date(startDate);
    var end = new Date(endDate);
    
    if (end < start) {
      g_form.showFieldMsg('end_date', 'End date must be after start date', 'error');
      g_form.setValue('end_date', '');
    } else {
      g_form.hideFieldMsg('end_date');
    }
  }
}

IncidentRouter.prototype = {
  initialize: function() {
    this.routingRules = this._loadRules();
  },
  
  determineGroup: function(incident) {
    // Check CI-based routing first
    if (!incident.cmdb_ci.nil()) {

      if (ciGroup) return ciGroup;
    }
    
    // Fall back to category-based routing

  _getGroupFromCI: function(ci) { /* ... */ },

title: Outage Prevention: Understanding Async Business Rule Risks and Scheduler Workers

Common Outage Causes

  • Slow ACL execution: Complex scripts in ACL conditions
  • Long-running scheduled jobs: Consuming scheduler workers
  • Async business rule backlogs: Queue overwhelming workers

Scheduler Worker Exhaustion

ServiceNow has 8 scheduler workers by default. When all are consumed:

  • SLA updates block
  • Event processing stops
  • Emails queue indefinitely
  • Async business rules backlog

Monitor Worker Usage

// Check scheduler worker status

Recursive Business Rule Prevention

// After Business Rule on incident
current.work_notes = 'Auto-updated';
current.update(); // Triggers this BR again!

// SAFE - use setWorkflow(false)
current.work_notes = 'Auto-updated';
current.setWorkflow(false); // Prevents BR trigger
current.update();

// SAFEST - use Event Queue for deferred processing
gs.eventQueue('incident.process', current, current.sys_id, '');
// Separate async BR responds to event

Event Queue Pattern for Delays

// Instead of gs.sleep() which blocks a worker:
// DON'T DO THIS:
gs.sleep(300000); // Blocks worker for 5 minutes!

// DO THIS - schedule future event:
gs.eventQueueScheduled('your.event.name', current, 'param1', 'param2', 
  new GlideDateTime().addSeconds(300));

Function Encapsulation

// Always enclose script in functions to prevent variable leakage
(function executeRule(current, previous) {
  // Variables scoped to this function
  var localVar = 'safe';
  
  // Your business logic here
  
})(current, previous);

// Without encapsulation, variables leak to global scope
// This can cause unpredictable behavior across transactions

ACL Performance

// SLOW ACL - complex query in script
// Runs on EVERY record access
var gr = new GlideRecord('sys_user_group');
gr.addQuery('members', 'CONTAINS', gs.getUserID());
gr.query(); // Query per record!

// FAST ACL - use roles and simple conditions
// Condition: current.assignment_group.manager == gs.getUserID()
// Or use: gs.hasRole('required_role')

Monitoring Dashboard Queries

// Key metrics to track
var metrics = {
  // Scheduler worker utilization
  activeWorkers: getActiveWorkerCount(),
  
  // Async queue health
  asyncQueueDepth: getAsyncQueueDepth(),
  asyncOldestJob: getOldestAsyncJob(),
  
  // Business rule health
  slowBRs: getSlowBusinessRules(),
  recursiveRisk: detectRecursiveRisk()
};

function getActiveWorkerCount() {
  var ga = new GlideAggregate('sys_trigger');
  ga.addQuery('state', 'executing');
  ga.addAggregate('COUNT');
  ga.query();
  ga.next();
  return ga.getAggregate('COUNT');
}

title: User Experience Analytics (UXA) in Yokohama: Complete Re-platforming Guide
excerpt: Yokohama completely redesigned User Experience Analytics with extended history, cross-app filtering, and new navigation paths. Learn the new capabilities and migration considerations.
content:
Major UXA Changes in Yokohama

UXA (App Scope: sn_uxa_dashboard, version 5.0.8) underwent a complete redesign:

  • Extended user history to two years (previously limited)
  • Cross-application view filtering
  • Granular event property filtering with new condition builder
  • Dashboard moved under Platform Analytics in All Menu
  • Navigation Paths replaces redundant "Users flow" feature

Captured Metrics

UXA captures across Next Experience apps, Virtual Agent, Service Portal, and Employee Center:

  • Page views
  • Average duration
  • Load times
  • Session analytics
  • Retention metrics
  • Navigation paths

Required Roles

RoleAccess Level
analytics_adminFull configuration
analytics_viewerView dashboards
sn_uxa_mobile_adminMobile analytics
sn_uxa_portal_adminPortal analytics
sn_uxa_core_adminCore UI analytics

Consent Policy Change

Important: Starting in Yokohama, "No Consent Required" is the default consent policy. This is significant for privacy-conscious implementations.

// Check current consent policy
var policy = gs.getProperty('sn_uxa.consent_policy');
gs.info('Current UXA consent policy: ' + policy);

// If you need opt-in consent:
gs.setProperty('sn_uxa.consent_policy', 'opt_in');

Querying UXA Data

// Get page view statistics
var pageViews = new GlideAggregate('sn_uxa_page_view');
pageViews.addQuery('sys_created_on', '>=', gs.daysAgo(30));
pageViews.addAggregate('COUNT');
pageViews.groupBy('page_id');
pageViews.orderByAggregate('COUNT', 'DESC');
pageViews.setLimit(10);
pageViews.query();

gs.info('Top 10 pages (last 30 days):');
while (pageViews.next()) {
  gs.info(pageViews.page_id + ': ' + pageViews.getAggregate('COUNT') + ' views');
}

Performance Analysis Pattern

// Identify slow-loading pages
var slowPages = new GlideRecord('sn_uxa_page_view');
slowPages.addQuery('load_time', '>', 3000); // > 3 seconds
slowPages.addQuery('sys_created_on', '>=', gs.daysAgo(7));
slowPages.query();

var pageStats = {};
while (slowPages.next()) {
  var pageId = slowPages.getValue('page_id');
  if (!pageStats[pageId]) {
    pageStats[pageId] = { count: 0, totalTime: 0 };
  }
  pageStats[pageId].count++;
  pageStats[pageId].totalTime += parseInt(slowPages.getValue('load_time'));
}

// Calculate average and report
for (var page in pageStats) {
  var avg = pageStats[page].totalTime / pageStats[page].count;
  gs.info('Slow page: ' + page + 
    ' | Occurrences: ' + pageStats[page].count +
    ' | Avg load time: ' + avg + 'ms');
}

Migration Considerations

  • Users flow reports need reconfiguration as Navigation Paths
  • Review consent settings for GDPR/privacy compliance
  • Update any reports using old UXA table structures
  • Verify role assignments include new specialized roles

title: Technical Debt Management: The 5% TDR Rule and Upgrade-Safe Development
excerpt: Keep technical debt under control with the 5% Technical Debt Ratio standard, upgrade-safe development patterns, and systematic remediation strategies.
content:
Technical Debt Warning Signs

  • Poor coding standards across team
  • Unclear code ownership
  • Bug rate exceeding closed rate
  • Health Scan scores not improving
  • Multiple teams on same code without coordination

The 5% TDR Standard

The Technical Debt Ratio (TDR) standard cap is 5%—higher indicates significant problems requiring immediate attention.

// Calculate simple TDR proxy
var findings = new GlideAggregate('sn_impact_ph_finding');
findings.addQuery('state', 'open');
findings.addAggregate('COUNT');
findings.query();
findings.next();
var openFindings = parseInt(findings.getAggregate('COUNT'));

var totalObjects = new GlideAggregate('sys_metadata');
totalObjects.addQuery('sys_scope', 'x_custom_app');
totalObjects.addAggregate('COUNT');
totalObjects.query();
totalObjects.next();
var totalCount = parseInt(totalObjects.getAggregate('COUNT'));

var tdr = (openFindings / totalCount) * 100;
gs.info('Technical Debt Ratio: ' + tdr.toFixed(2) + '%');

if (tdr > 5) {
  gs.warn('TDR exceeds 5% threshold - remediation required');
}

Configure Before Customize Principle

Risk hierarchy for modifications:

Change TypeRisk LevelGuidance
Form layout changesMinimalSafe to modify
UI Policy additionsLowPreferred approach
New Business RulesLowKeep scoped
Modified Business RulesMediumClone and modify
Baseline Script Include modsHighAvoid - extend instead
Core table modificationsVery HighCreate extension tables

Upgrade-Safe Checklist

  • Never modify baseline/OOTB records—create new or extend
  • Use scoped applications for custom functionality
  • Preview update sets before committing to identify conflicts
  • Review skipped records after each upgrade cycle
  • Document all customizations and their business justification

Extension Pattern

// Instead of modifying baseline Script Include:
// DON'T: Edit IncidentUtils directly

// DO: Create extension in your scope
var IncidentUtilsExtended = Class.create();
IncidentUtilsExtended.prototype = Object.extendsObject(IncidentUtils, {
  
  // Override specific method
  getAssignmentGroup: function(incident) {
    // Custom logic first
    var customGroup = this._customRouting(incident);
    if (customGroup) {
      return customGroup;
    }
    
    // Fall back to baseline behavior
    return IncidentUtils.prototype.getAssignmentGroup.call(this, incident);
  },
  
  // Add new methods
  _customRouting: function(incident) {
    // Your custom logic here
    return null;
  },
  
  type: 'IncidentUtilsExtended'
});

Update Set Conflict Resolution

// Pre-commit conflict check
var conflicts = new GlideRecord('sys_update_preview_problem');
conflicts.addQuery('remote_update_set', 'UPDATE_SET_SYS_ID');
conflicts.addQuery('type', 'conflict');
conflicts.query();

while (conflicts.next()) {
  gs.warn('Conflict detected: ' + conflicts.description);
  gs.info('Affected record: ' + conflicts.remote_update.name);
  gs.info('Resolution needed: ' + conflicts.disposition);
}

Remediation Prioritization

  1. Security vulnerabilities: Immediate
  2. Performance impacts: Within sprint
  3. Upgrade blockers: Before next upgrade
  4. Maintainability issues: Quarterly cleanup
  5. Code style violations: Opportunistic

title: ServiceNow Developer Core APIs & Platform Fundamentals (Zurich/Yokohama Era)
excerpt: Practical reference to current ServiceNow server-side and integration APIs with a focus on core primitives, Flow Designer internals, performance, and security fundamentals for scoped app developers.
content:
Overview

This reference distills current ServiceNow platform fundamentals for developers building scalable, upgrade-safe applications and integrations. It focuses on the Glide server APIs, integration primitives, Flow Designer behavior, performance patterns, and security concepts that remain stable across recent releases (Zurich/Yokohama generation).

Core Server-Side APIs

GlideRecord

Purpose: Synchronous CRUD and querying on tables; primary server-side data API.

Core usage pattern

// Query incidents with state=2 (In Progress) and short_description contains keyword
var gr = new GlideRecord('incident');
gr.addQuery('state', 2);
gr.addQuery('short_description', 'CONTAINS', 'network');
gr.query();
while (gr.next()) {
  gs.info('Incident: ' + gr.number + ' - ' + gr.short_description);
}

GlideAggregate

Purpose: Efficient COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX operations without loading full records.

// Count active incidents by priority
var ga = new GlideAggregate('incident');
ga.addQuery('active', true);
ga.addAggregate('COUNT');
ga.groupBy('priority');
ga.query();
while (ga.next()) {
  gs.info('Priority ' + ga.priority + ': ' + ga.getAggregate('COUNT'));
}

GlideRecord Best Practices

  • Use GlideAggregate for counts and sums instead of looping through GlideRecord results.
  • Always add appropriate query filters to limit result sets.
  • Use setLimit() when you only need a subset of records.
  • Avoid dot-walking in loops; cache reference values before iteration.

Integration APIs

RESTMessageV2

Purpose: Outbound REST calls to external systems with authentication, headers, and payload management.

// Outbound REST call with OAuth 2.0
var rm = new sn_ws.RESTMessageV2('My_REST_Message', 'POST');
rm.setStringParameterNoEscape('endpoint', 'https://api.example.com/data');
rm.setRequestHeader('Content-Type', 'application/json');
rm.setRequestBody(JSON.stringify({ key: 'value' }));

var response = rm.execute();
var httpStatus = response.getStatusCode();
var body = response.getBody();

if (httpStatus == 200) {
  var parsed = JSON.parse(body);
  gs.info('Response: ' + parsed.result);
} else {
  gs.error('REST call failed: ' + httpStatus);
}

Scripted REST APIs

Purpose: Expose custom inbound REST endpoints for external systems to call ServiceNow.

// Scripted REST Resource (GET method)
(function process(request, response) {
  var incidentId = request.pathParams.id;
  var gr = new GlideRecord('incident');
  
  if (gr.get(incidentId)) {
    response.setStatus(200);
    response.setBody({
      number: gr.number.toString(),
      short_description: gr.short_description.toString(),
      state: gr.state.getDisplayValue()
    });
  } else {
    response.setStatus(404);
    response.setBody({ error: 'Incident not found' });
  }
})(request, response);

Flow Designer Internals

Execution Context

Flow Designer flows execute in a dedicated context with access to trigger data, input variables, and step outputs. Understanding execution boundaries is critical for debugging.

  • Trigger context: Contains the record or event that initiated the flow.
  • Step outputs: Each action step produces outputs accessible to subsequent steps via data pills.
  • Transaction boundaries: By default, flows run in a single transaction; use async subflows to break transaction scope.

Error Handling Patterns

// Script step with try-catch for external calls
(function execute(inputs, outputs) {
  try {
    var rm = new sn_ws.RESTMessageV2('External_API', 'GET');
    var response = rm.execute();
    
    if (response.getStatusCode() != 200) {
      outputs.success = false;
      outputs.error_message = 'API returned ' + response.getStatusCode();
      return;
    }
    
    outputs.success = true;
    outputs.data = JSON.parse(response.getBody());
  } catch (e) {
    outputs.success = false;
    outputs.error_message = e.message;
  }
})(inputs, outputs);

Subflow Reuse

Extract common logic into subflows for reusability. Subflows can be called from multiple parent flows and accept input/output variables.

  • Use subflows for: notifications, approvals, assignment logic, external API calls.
  • Keep subflows focused on a single responsibility.
  • Version subflows carefully—changes affect all calling flows.

Performance Patterns

Query Optimization

  • Use indexes: Query on indexed fields (sys_id, number, active, state) for fast lookups.
  • Avoid wildcard starts: CONTAINS and STARTSWITH are efficient; avoid patterns like ENDSWITH which cannot use indexes.
  • Limit results: Always use setLimit() when you need only a subset of records.
// Efficient: Query on indexed field with limit
var gr = new GlideRecord('incident');
gr.addQuery('active', true);
gr.addQuery('priority', 1);
gr.orderByDesc('sys_created_on');
gr.setLimit(50);
gr.query();

Async Processing

Move heavy operations to background processing to avoid blocking user transactions.

// Schedule heavy work asynchronously
var worker = new GlideScriptedHierarchicalWorker();
worker.setProgressName('Bulk CI Update');
worker.setScriptIncludeName('BulkCIProcessor');
worker.setScriptIncludeMethod('process');
worker.putMethodArg('batchSize', 500);
worker.setBackground(true);
worker.start();

Caching Strategies

  • Use GlideSystem cache for frequently accessed configuration data.
  • Cache reference field values before loops to avoid repeated database calls.
  • Leverage system properties (gs.getProperty()) which are automatically cached.

Security Fundamentals

ACL Evaluation Order

ServiceNow evaluates ACLs in a specific order. Understanding this prevents security gaps.

  1. Table-level ACLs (e.g., incident.*)
  2. Field-level ACLs (e.g., incident.work_notes)
  3. Row-level conditions within ACLs

ACLs are AND-ed together: a user must pass ALL applicable ACLs to access a record or field.

Scoped Application Security

  • Application scope: Isolates custom tables, scripts, and configurations from global scope.
  • Cross-scope access: Requires explicit access grants via Application Cross-Scope Access records.
  • Script Include access: Mark Script Includes as Client Callable only when necessary; prefer server-side calls.
// Check user role before sensitive operation
if (!gs.hasRole('admin') && !gs.hasRole('itil')) {
  gs.addErrorMessage('Insufficient privileges for this operation');
  current.setAbortAction(true);
  return;
}

API Access Controls

  • Scripted REST APIs inherit table ACLs by default; add explicit role requirements for sensitive endpoints.
  • Use OAuth 2.0 or token-based auth for external integrations instead of basic auth.
  • Audit API access via Transaction Logs and API Usage Analytics.

Common Anti-Patterns

  • Querying without filters: Never call gr.query() without adding conditions on large tables.
  • Dot-walking in loops: Cache reference values before iteration to avoid N+1 query problems.
  • Synchronous external calls in Business Rules: Move external API calls to async flows or scheduled jobs.
  • Hardcoding sys_ids: Use system properties or reference fields instead of hardcoded identifiers.
  • Ignoring transaction limits: Be aware of the 10,000 record and 300-second transaction limits in synchronous operations.

Conclusion

Mastering these core APIs, Flow Designer patterns, performance techniques, and security fundamentals provides the foundation for building enterprise-grade ServiceNow applications. Focus on indexed queries, async processing for heavy workloads, proper ACL design, and modular flow architecture to ensure your solutions scale reliably across Zurich, Yokohama, and future releases.

title: Building on ServiceNow's Latest AI: Now Assist, AI Control Tower, and Agentic Patterns for Developers
excerpt: Explore the newest ServiceNow AI capabilities—from Now Assist model v2.0 and AI Control Tower to Virtual Agent, AI Search, and agent-to-agent patterns. Learn concrete implementation techniques using GlideRecord and Flow Designer so you can safely plug GenAI and LLMs into real workflows.
content:
Overview

ServiceNow continues to expand its AI Platform with deeper GenAI, safer orchestration, and richer virtual agent capabilities. Recent releases introduce upgraded Now Assist models, enhanced governance with AI Control Tower, and new agentic automation patterns that span workflows and external LLMs.

For developers, the value is twofold: you can now embed powerful AI into everyday flows (summaries, routing, answers) while keeping strict control over data, models, and observability. This article focuses on practical implementation patterns using GlideRecord, Flow Designer, and out-of-box AI components.

Now Assist and GenAI Updates

ServiceNow's new AI models and Now Assist experiences deliver better summarization, answer quality, and workspace integration across ITSM, CSM, HR, and Employee Center.

Key capabilities

  • Now Assist models v2.0 with improved intent understanding, summarization, and adherence to platform security boundaries.
  • Embedded GenAI in workspaces for incident, case, and knowledge summarization, draft responses, and content generation.
  • Knowledge Center with AI-assisted editing for faster article creation and refinement.

Actionable implementation pattern: AI-driven incident summary

Typical flow:

  1. Agent opens an incident in Workspace.
  2. Now Assist generates a summary from activity and related records.
  3. Agent optionally stores the summary back on the record.

To persist a GenAI-generated summary using GlideRecord in a Script Action or Script Include:

// Called from a UI Action or Flow Designer Action when the agent accepts a Now Assist summary
(function(storeSummary) {
  if (!storeSummary.incident_sys_id || !storeSummary.summary_text)
    return;

  var gr = new GlideRecord('incident');
  if (gr.get(storeSummary.incident_sys_id)) {
    gr.u_ai_summary = storeSummary.summary_text; // Custom field to store AI output
    gr.update();
  }
})({
  incident_sys_id: current.sys_id,
  summary_text: inputs.summary // Passed from Flow or UI
});

Best practice: persist only necessary AI outputs (e.g., summary, classification) and avoid storing raw prompts or sensitive content.

AI Control Tower and Predictive Intelligence

AI Control Tower centralizes model selection, governance, and observability for Now Assist, Predictive Intelligence, and integrated LLMs. Predictive Intelligence continues to power auto-routing, auto-classification, and recommendations.

Control Tower patterns

  • Define per-use-case policies (e.g., which LLM for summarization vs. classification).
  • Enable logging and guardrails for prompts and responses (mask PII where required).
  • Route traffic between Now LLM and partner models (e.g., Microsoft, OpenAI) while retaining platform security controls.

Predictive Intelligence auto-routing in Flow Designer

Example: Classify and route new incidents using a trained model, then fall back to business rules if confidence is low.

// Script step in Flow Designer: Evaluate PI classification confidence
var gr = new GlideRecord('incident');
if (!gr.get(current.sys_id)) {
  outputs.is_confident = false;
  return;
}

// Assume a classification result is stored by an OOB PI action
var confidence = parseFloat(gr.u_pi_confidence || 0);
outputs.is_confident = confidence >= 0.8;

Then use a Flow Designer Decision:

  • If is_confident == true → set assignment group from PI prediction.
  • Else → route to default triage queue.

Virtual Agent AI and NLU Updates

Virtual Agent leverages updated NLU and GenAI to handle more complex dialogs, summarize conversations, and draft resolutions.

Patterns to implement

  • Use topic triggers that rely on new NLU models for broader intent coverage.
  • Call Now Assist within a Virtual Agent topic to summarize the chat and store it on the associated record.
  • Attach GenAI-generated resolution text to incident or case work notes from within the topic.

Example: Virtual Agent topic script to persist a GenAI chat summary:

// In a VA Script step (Client callable Script Include pattern)
var VaAiUtils = Class.create();
VaAiUtils.prototype = {
  initialize: function() {},

  saveSummaryToIncident: function(incidentId, summary) {
    if (!incidentId || !summary)
      return false;

    var inc = new GlideRecord('incident');
    if (!inc.get(incidentId))
      return false;

    inc.work_notes = 'AI chat summary:\n' + summary;
    inc.update();
    return true;
  },

  type: 'VaAiUtils'
};

Agent-to-Agent (A2A), MCP, and LLM Integration

ServiceNow's agentic vision includes AI agents that collaborate with human agents and external systems. Through AI Control Tower and partner integrations (e.g., Microsoft), you can orchestrate multi-agent workflows while keeping governance centralized.

Agent-to-Agent & MCP patterns

  • Use Flow Designer to orchestrate calls between Now Assist, external LLMs, and internal APIs.
  • Configure AI Control Tower policies to direct which agent or LLM owns each task (classification, summarization, content generation).
  • Integrate with Microsoft collaboration surfaces so AI agents can coordinate resolutions from Teams while updating ServiceNow records.

Example: Flow Designer orchestrated multi-agent flow

  1. Trigger: Incident created.
  2. Action 1: Now Assist summarizes description and context.
  3. Action 2: Predictive Intelligence suggests assignment group.
  4. Action 3: External LLM via HTTP step drafts a customer-facing update.
  5. Action 4: GlideRecord step stores outputs and posts a work note.
// Example Script step in Flow Designer combining AI outputs
(function execute(inputs, outputs) {
  var inc = new GlideRecord('incident');
  if (!inc.get(current.sys_id))
    return;

  // Inputs from previous AI actions
  var aiSummary = inputs.ai_summary || '';
  var aiReply   = inputs.ai_reply || '';

  if (aiSummary)
    inc.u_ai_summary = aiSummary;

  if (aiReply)
    inc.comments = 'Suggested reply (AI):\n' + aiReply;

  inc.update();
})(inputs, outputs);

LLM Integration Patterns and AI Search

ServiceNow supports flexible LLM choices through AI Control Tower, plus AI Search to provide semantic, relevance-ranked results across knowledge and records.

Recommended patterns

  • Use AI Search as the primary entry point for AI-powered Q&A instead of calling LLMs directly for data retrieval.
  • Combine AI Search results + Now Assist to generate grounded answers that reference specific articles or records.
  • Configure index sources carefully (knowledge, catalog, cases) to avoid exposing sensitive data.

Example: Scripted AI Search query + answer generation pattern

// Pseudo-pattern: use AI Search for grounding, then pass snippets to GenAI
var query = 'reset VPN password';
var searchGr = new GlideRecord('sa_ai_search_result');
searchGr.addQuery('query_string', query);
searchGr.query();

var snippets = [];
while (searchGr.next() && snippets.length < 3) {
  snippets.push(searchGr.getValue('snippet')); // Hypothetical field
}

// Concatenate snippets and send to a Now Assist or LLM action via Flow
outputs.context_snippets = snippets.join('\n---\n');

Best Practices

  • Start with high-value, low-risk use cases like summaries, routing, and draft responses before moving to autonomous actions.
  • Use AI Control Tower for every production GenAI use case to manage providers, guardrails, and observability.
  • Keep prompts and outputs minimal and avoid sending unnecessary fields or PII to external models.
  • Ground GenAI with AI Search and concrete record data to improve accuracy and reduce hallucinations.
  • Capture metrics (accept/override, resolution time, CSAT) to continuously tune Predictive Intelligence and Now Assist configurations.
  • Use Script Includes as thin AI facades so flows, UI Actions, and Virtual Agent topics share the same logic.

Common Pitfalls

  • Calling LLMs directly for system-of-record queries instead of using AI Search or GlideRecord, leading to inaccurate or stale answers.
  • Bypassing AI Control Tower and hardcoding provider endpoints, which breaks governance, observability, and future portability.
  • Overloading prompts with entire records (including sensitive fields) rather than narrowing to relevant attributes.
  • Letting AI auto-update records without human review for high-risk actions like approvals, major incident communication, or HR decisions.
  • Ignoring model versioning when moving to newer Now Assist models, resulting in untested behavior changes in production workflows.
  • Embedding complex business logic inside prompts (" do X except Y") instead of enforcing rules in GlideRecord scripts and Flow conditions.

title: New Integration Patterns, Flow Designer Tips, and Integration Hub Updates for ServiceNow Developers
excerpt: Practical guidance on current ServiceNow integration patterns, actionable Flow Designer tips, and recent Integration Hub capabilities to accelerate reliable, maintainable integrations.
content:
Overview — What's Changed and Why It Matters

ServiceNow integration patterns continue to converge on three goals: make integrations more resilient at scale, reduce custom code, and enable real-time or near-real-time data flows via streaming where appropriate.

Updated Integration Patterns to Use

  • API-first flow (REST/Scripted REST) for synchronous interactions: Use when a synchronous response is required. For example, create a Scripted REST API to handle synchronous updates from external systems. Here's a practical example of a Scripted REST resource that processes incoming incident data:
    • var IncidentAPI = Class.create();
IncidentAPI.prototype = Object.extendsObject(AbstractAjaxProcessor, {
    createIncident: function() {
        var short_desc = this.getParameter('sysparm_short_description');
        var caller_id = this.getParameter('sysparm_caller_id');
        
        var gr = new GlideRecord('incident');
        gr.initialize();
        gr.short_description = short_desc;
        gr.caller_id = caller_id;
        var sys_id = gr.insert();
        
        return 'Incident created with sys_id: ' + sys_id;
    },
    
    type: 'IncidentAPI'
});
  • Event/Stream-based for high-volume or low-latency needs: Use Stream Connect or message producers for telemetry. Publish events using GlideEventManager for real-time notifications in high-volume scenarios.
  • ETL/Batch for bulk data and CMDB population: Use Integration Hub ETL actions for large imports. A GlideRecord example for bulk CMDB updates might look like this, ensuring efficient querying and updates:
    • var ciGr = new GlideRecord('cmdb_ci_server');
ciGr.addQuery('name', 'IN', bulkNames.join(','));
ciGr.query();
while (ciGr.next()) {
    ciGr.u_last_scan_date = new GlideDateTime();
    ciGr.u_scan_status = 'Complete';
    ciGr.update();
}
  • Process API + Orchestration for cross-system workflows: Create lightweight process APIs that encapsulate business rules.

Practical Flow Designer Tips

  • Prefer subflows and reusable flow actions: Encapsulate repeated logic into subflows or custom actions. In a custom Script Step within Flow Designer, you can use GlideRecord for reusable data operations, such as updating a related record:
    • (function execute(inputs, outputs) {
    var triggerRecord = inputs.trigger_record; // Data pill from trigger
    
    var gr = new GlideRecord('incident');
    if (gr.get(triggerRecord.sys_id)) {
        gr.state = 6; // Resolved
        gr.close_notes = 'Resolved via Flow Designer subflow';
        gr.update();
        outputs.resolved_incident = gr.getUniqueValue();
    }
})(inputs, outputs);
  • Implement defensive error handling: Add retry policies, exponential backoff, and compensating flows. Use Script Steps to log errors and trigger notifications.
  • Leverage dynamic inputs/outputs: Use introspection-capable actions to reduce maintenance. For dynamic REST calls in Flow Designer, reference data pills directly in REST Message actions.
  • Test with both unit and integration scenarios: Create mock REST endpoints and automate flow tests. Mock endpoints can simulate external APIs during testing.

Integration Hub Updates

  • Starter Package: Basic SOAP/REST steps, JDBC, PowerShell, SFTP/SSH. These provide out-of-the-box actions for common integrations without custom scripting.
  • Professional Package: Advanced features like introspection for dynamic data handling. Introspection allows Flow Designer actions to automatically map fields from external APIs, minimizing hardcoded configurations.

By adopting these patterns and tips, developers can build more scalable integrations while minimizing custom code maintenance. For instance, combining API-first flows with Flow Designer subflows enables orchestrated, resilient processes across systems. Always test flows thoroughly using the built-in execution details to verify data flow and error handling.

title: This Week in Enterprise AI: GenAI, LLMs, and Agents — Practical Takeaways for ServiceNow Developers
excerpt: Major vendors released model and agent updates this week that push multimodal reasoning, cheaper inference, and agent-first integrations. ServiceNow developers should focus on connectors, orchestration, security, and observability.

Key Developments and What They Mean

This week saw coordinated advances from major AI vendors emphasizing multimodal LLMs, lower-cost inference, and agentic capabilities that are moving autonomous workflows from experiments into production.

  • Multimodal, higher-reasoning models are now mainstream — Vendors announced new multimodal releases with improved reasoning and coding skills, enabling agents to process text, images, and structured data seamlessly for richer ServiceNow integrations.
  • Agent-first features accelerate automation — Agent capabilities like long-horizon planning, tool use, and parallel thought streams are being prioritized, allowing developers to build production-grade AI agents directly into ServiceNow workflows.
  • Costs and performance improve — Recent launches include lower-priced model variants and faster inference tiers, making scalable AI adoption feasible for enterprise ServiceNow projects without prohibitive expenses.

Top Practical Actions for ServiceNow Projects

ServiceNow developers should prioritize connectors, orchestration, security, and observability to leverage these advancements effectively. Here's how to implement them with code examples and best practices.

  • Design agent interfaces, not just prompts — Define a clear agent contract: input context, allowed tools, retry/timeout policies. Use Flow Designer or IntegrationHub to orchestrate agent execution. 
    // Example: agent request payload
{
  "intent": "summarize_incident",
  "context": {
    "incident_id": "INC0012345",
    "priority": "P2"
  },
  "tools": ["getIncident", "updateWorkNotes"],
  "timeoutMs": 15000
}
  • Build AI connectors as first-class integrations — Wrap LLM and agent APIs in Scripted REST APIs or IntegrationHub spokes. Centralize authentication, rate limiting, and error handling. 
    // Script Include snippet
var r = new sn_ws.RESTMessageV2('AI Provider', 'execute');
r.setRequestBody(JSON.stringify(payload));
var response = r.execute();
  • Enforce guardrails and security — Treat agents like privileged users. Scope data access with ACLs, sanitize inputs, and log all agent actions for auditability.
  • Add observability early — Log prompts, tool calls, token usage, latency, and failures to custom tables. This enables tuning, cost tracking, and compliance reviews.

Bottom Line

Enterprise AI is rapidly shifting toward agent-driven, multimodal workflows. For ServiceNow developers, the competitive advantage comes from strong orchestration, secure integrations, and production-grade observability — not from prompt engineering alone.
